title: The Empty Display Case
brief:
It is 18:08. The gold medal “Morgenstern” is missing. The authenticated sensor dates the removal by hand to 18:04:00 in the Gallery. Examine the four people who remained. Independent evidence will help you solve the case.

Your task: Choose exactly one of the four people as the person who removed the medal by hand. The evidence helps you deduce. A complete correct answer solves the case even without collected or cited evidence. An unsolved verdict means that the submitted answer does not yet fulfil the case task; it does not point out which individual statements are wrong.

Locations: Gallery – the empty display case and the visitor records. Courtyard – the area of the photo shoot. Archive – supervision, work records and key management. Workshop – restoration and transport materials. Foyer – closing and attendance list.

Your actions: search locations, ask people the available structured questions, read out released device evidence and submit a complete answer. Newly known entities can make further questions or evidence available. Questions and investigations can be repeated; in this first case they cost neither time nor points.

Statements made by people belong in the report journal. Independent observations are kept separate. A refusal to talk and a mere earlier visit are not proof of guilt.
challengeQuestion: Who removed the medal by hand?

labels.label: Discovery of the empty display case
Max Brandt
labels.role: historian and representative of the former owners' family

questionTexts.text: Were you in the Gallery at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: I won't comment on that. Ask someone else.

questionTexts.text: Did Max remove the medal by hand?
questionTexts.answer: Max? No, he didn't.

questionTexts.text: Were you in the Workshop at 18:05?
questionTexts.answer: Yes, at 18:05 I was in my workshop, at my workbench.

questionTexts.text: Was Nora in the Courtyard at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: Whether Nora was in the courtyard? I can't tell you that.

questionTexts.text: Would you like to comment on the removal?
questionTexts.answer: I have nothing to say about the medal.

questionTexts.text: Were you in the Gallery at 18:02?
questionTexts.answer: Yes, at 18:02 I was in the gallery, I admit that freely.

questionTexts.text: Were you in the Gallery at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: No! By 18:04 I was long gone.

questionTexts.text: Were you in the Courtyard at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: Yes, at 18:04 I was standing in the courtyard.

questionTexts.text: Was Lina in the Gallery at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: How should I know? I wasn't there.

questionTexts.text: Where is the complete photo evidence?
questionTexts.answer: Filmed? I know nothing about that, you'll have to ask Nora.

questionTexts.text: Was Max in the Courtyard at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: Yes, Max was standing with me in the courtyard at 18:04.

questionTexts.text: Were you in the Courtyard at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: Yes, I was in the courtyard taking photos.

questionTexts.text: Can I see the complete footage of this courtyard photo shoot?
questionTexts.answer: Yes, the camera ran the whole time. I always let it run during a shoot.

questionTexts.text: Was Max in the Gallery at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: No, he wasn't in the gallery, he was standing right next to me.

questionTexts.text: Was Lina in the Gallery at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: Lina? Hm. I was outside, I can't say for sure.

questionTexts.text: Was Max in the Gallery at 18:02?
questionTexts.answer: Indeed, Mr Brandt was in the gallery at 18:02.

questionTexts.text: Was Max in the Gallery at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: Indeed. At 18:04 Mr Brandt was in the gallery, I am quite certain.

questionTexts.text: Were you in the Archive at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: Indeed, I was in the archive at my work.

questionTexts.text: Where is the independent archive evidence?
questionTexts.answer: Indeed, the archive has a logging device. Whoever works there is in it.

questionTexts.text: Was Lina with you in the Archive at 18:03?
questionTexts.answer: Indeed, Ms Kern came to see me in the archive at 18:03.

publicRules.text: In this case, the image evidence released as observations is unaltered and synchronised with the removal sensor. Witness statements can be mistaken. A visit at a different time and a refusal to talk do not prove a removal by hand.
Only Max, Lina, Nora and Oskar come into question as the direct remover. There was exactly one direct remover. If three are ruled out, the fourth person remains.
The medal was removed by hand by a single person in the Gallery at 18:04:00. Anyone who was demonstrably at a different location at exactly that moment is ruled out as the direct remover.

epilogue:
Lina Kern gives up. At 18:04 she took the gold medal “Morgenstern” out of the display case herself and, one minute later, placed it in the transport case in the Workshop. She wanted to hide an unauthorised repair before the lender inspected the medal the next morning.

Max Brandt was in the Gallery at 18:02, but at the time of the theft he was standing with Nora Weiss in the Courtyard, as the complete courtyard footage shows. Oskar Falk was honestly mistaken when he saw Max in the Gallery at 18:04: the archive camera shows Oskar himself in the Archive at that very minute. The medal is in the transport case in the Workshop.
